en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on House-Shapes, 48.
The Training Rule on Lodging Houses.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā set out on a wandering tour without having assigned her lodging.
At that time, the lodging belonging to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was burning down.
The bhikkhunīs said this:
“Come, ladies, let us take out our belongings.
Some said, “We will not take them out, lady.”
“Whatever has been lost, he will surely accuse us of it all.
Then the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having returned once more to that lodging, asked the bhikkhunīs:
“Noble ladies, have you brought out the belongings?”
“We did not take it out, noble lady.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā complained, criticized, and spread it about:
“How can these bhikkhunīs fail to take out their belongings when the lodging is on fire?”
Those bhikkhunīs who were modest … [as above] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā set out on a journey without first relinquishing her lodging? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā sets out on a journey without first relinquishing her lodging?”

“It is true, Blessed One. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “… How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā set out on a journey without having relinquished her lodging? This is not for the benefit of the bhikkhunīs…” [as before] … “In many ways, monks, have I spoken in praise of restraint, moderation, and contentment. It is not, monks, for the benefit of the bhikkhunīs that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā sets out on a journey without having relinquished her lodging. Therefore, monks, this training rule should be recited thus: ‘If a bhikkhunī, without having relinquished her lodging, goes away on a journey, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, does a bhikkhunī relinquish her lodging? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. If she departs without having relinquished it in this way, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, does a bhikkhunī not relinquish her lodging? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, not relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should not relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. If she departs without having relinquished it in this way, she commits an offense of wrong-doing. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, is a lodging relinquished? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. In this way, monks, a lodging is relinquished. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, is a lodging not relinquished? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, not relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should not relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. In this way, monks, a lodging is not relinquished. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, is a lodging relinquished by one who is departing? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. In this way, monks, a lodging is relinquished by one who is departing. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, is a lodging not relinquished by one who is departing? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, not relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should not relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. In this way, monks, a lodging is not relinquished by one who is departing. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, is a lodging relinquished by one who is departing while leaving behind some belongings? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. In this way, monks, a lodging is relinquished by one who is departing while leaving behind some belongings. [The Blessed One further said: “And how, monks, is a lodging not relinquished by one who is departing while leaving behind some belongings? Therein, monks, a bhikkhunī who has been staying in a lodging should, when departing, not relinquish it to another bhikkhunī, or to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a group of bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no other bhikkhunī, she should not relinquish it to a male lay follower, or to a female lay follower, or to a male novice, or to a female novice, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to you. If there is no one else at all, she should not relinquish it to the four quarters, saying: ‘I relinquish this lodging to the four quarters. In this way, monks, a lodging is not relinquished by one who is departing while leaving behind some belongings
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:
‘If any nun, without having relinquished her dwelling, should set out on a journey, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such...
"nun" means... [as before].
...pe... this is the "bhikkhunī" intended in this context.
A "dwelling place" (āvasatha) is said to be that which is fitted with a door-panel.
"Should she set out on a journey without having made an assignment":

for a nun, a trainee nun, or a female novice who sets out on a journey without having made an assignment, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) when she crosses beyond the enclosure of an enclosed dwelling;
there is an offense of expiation when she crosses beyond the precinct of an unenclosed dwelling.
If she departs when [the robe] has not been relinquished, perceiving that it has not been relinquished, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she departs when [the robe] has not been relinquished, but is uncertain of it, there is an offense of expiation.
If she departs when [the robe] has not been relinquished, perceiving that it has been relinquished, there is an offense of expiation.
If one departs without having relinquished that which is secured by a door-bolt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it has been relinquished, but one perceives it as not having been relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it has been relinquished, but one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she has relinquished it, and she perceives that she has relinquished it, there is no offense.
There is no offense if,
having relinquished it, she departs.
If there is an obstacle,
or if she has searched but not found [a preceptor],
or if she is ill.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for one who is a first-time offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
